newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commissioner to chat with public on Internet.
newsitem.headline: EU Commissioner to chat with public on Internet.

text.p: Worried about how the European Union will cope with admitting former foes from eastern Europe? Or whether a border-free Europe will mean you have more chance of coming up against organised crime mafias?
Or curious about how the Union can help create jobs or how a single European money will affect your mortgage or the price of carrots?
Then call http://europa.eu.int/chat.htm to get on the list for a Europe-wide internet chat with the EU's Culture Commissioner Marcelino Oreja next Tuesday.
The European Commission said Oreja will have a two-hour long chat with the public on the Internet starting at 1700 GMT next Tuesday.
The discussion will take place in ten out of 11 EU official languages, from Finnish to Portuguese, but not Greek which has a different alphabet.
"This will be the first time that a member of the European Commission engages in direct dialogue with the public on the Internet," the Commission said in a statement on Thursday.
"In the second place the multilingual nature of the exchange represents an unprecedented event for the Internet."
